one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with a parish-priest homily about obedience without satisfaction in 23 years of priestly assignments, and an autobiographical recollection of his late father redirecting him from chemical engineering to law just before passing away in his first year of prelaw -- establishing the column's frame: our decisions in life are limited by attendant facts, rules, goals, means, and time. He applies this frame to Jan 20, 2001. Given the choice between actively defending the Constitution and rule of law on one hand, and passively allowing chaos, revolutionary government, dictatorship, or coup d'état on the other, the SC 'courageously chose the first option, to defend the Constitution and the rule of law.' As he put it in a speech, 'The Court descended from its lofty perch on Mt. Olympus to avert a civil strife and to save our constitutional system from collapse.' Though initially incredulous, his colleagues -- after careful weighing -- agreed unanimously to authorize CJ Davide to induct the VP as 'acting president,' with an oath prepared by Justice Bernardo Pardo. This is why, when ambushed by media just before noon of Jan 20, Davide announced he was going to the Edsa Shrine 'to induct the vice president as acting president.' At the shrine, emcee Vicky Garchitorena announced each justice; the crowd chanted 'Da-vi-de, Da-vi-de, Da-vi-de' in awe of his impeachment-trial performance. Arroyo was sworn in at 12:29 pm on Saturday, Jan 20 -- using Pardo's prepared oath but with the word 'acting' orally omitted by both Davide and Arroyo. At the usual Monday breakfast on Jan 22, three justices who had been out of town on the crucial Jan 20 but had given their telephoned consent to the 'acting' oath were livid. Davide arrived at noon (he had been guest speaker elsewhere), acknowledged the consensus to swear in Arroyo as acting president, but explained that taking into account the confluence of events, he had decided on the spot to omit reading the word 'acting' -- ever a gentleman, he humbly took full responsibility for the omission. After heated debate, the 15 justices agreed 'unanimously to CONFIRM the authority given by the twelve (12) members of the Court then present to the Chief Justice on January 20, 2001 to administer the oath of office to Vice President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo as President ... without prejudice to the disposition of any justiciable case which may be filed by a proper party.' That justiciable case came when Estrada sued to stop Ombudsman Desierto from criminal indictment, claiming presidential immunity on the theory that he was president-on-leave and Arroyo was only acting president. The case revolved around Sec. 8, Art. VII: 'In case of death, permanent disability, removal from office, or resignation of the President, the Vice President shall become the President.' Justice Puno's path-breaking ponencia explained that resignation can be oral or written, express or implied, and applied the totality test: 'the totality of prior, contemporaneous and posterior facts and circumstantial evidence bearing a material relevance on the issue' established that Estrada had resigned. The decision traced the 'authoritative window' to his mind: political isolation, Angara's diary indicating intent to give up the presidency, negotiations for graceful and dignified exit and peaceful transfer of power, acknowledgment of Arroyo's oath, leaving Malacañang, expression of gratitude to the people. Panganiban closes with a rebuttal: those interested in the truth should read Estrada vs Desierto carefully before criticizing -- and those who peddle the falsehood that Panganiban concocted 'constructive resignation' could learn a lesson in the responsible use of free speech. True, he proposed the oath-taking and joined the 'acting president' consensus, but having inhibited in Desierto vs Estrada (after Saguisag's petition), he could not have espoused the resignation theory; ascribing it falsely is the actual offense. He ends with a forward-pointer to Estrada's post-pardon question about appointee 'ingratitude.'
